conventional.policy_description: Raise corporate rate from 21% to 28%. Treasury estimate (FY2025 Green Book): raises ~\$1.35T over 10 years.

credibility.own_row_caption: Unfitted reconstruction, 29.1% from -$1.35T (U.S. Treasury) — no constant is fitted to this figure.
limitations: holdout labels follow the locked post-2026-05-02 regression protocol; they are not retroactive historical out-of-sample claims.
Corporate base-shifting, pass-through spillovers, and international interactions are simplified relative to Treasury and JCT models.

The target prices a broader reform than the model builds. Treasury's FY2025 Green Book chapter (report p. 2) states 'The effective global intangible low-taxed income (GILTI) rate would increase to 14 percent under the proposal', and every edition since FY2023 carries that step inside the corporate-rate row, while the factory scored against it sets gilti_rate_change=0.0. The GILTI leg is never printed separately and cannot be differenced across editions, so the reported error measures a scope mismatch as well as a fit.
Poor, and reclassified rather than retuned: `BASELINE_TAXABLE_PROFITS_BILLIONS` is fitted so the `reported` path lands on this target, and the scorecard / app score `derived`.

The target is a rate-PLUS-GILTI row scored against a rate-only shape. Treasury's FY2025 Green Book chapter (report p. 2) says 'The effective global intangible low-taxed income (GILTI) rate would increase to 14 percent under the proposal', and every edition from FY2023 carries that step, while `create_biden_corporate_rate_only` sets `gilti_rate_change=0.0`. The GILTI leg's size is never printed and cannot be recovered by differencing editions, so the error measures a scope mismatch as well as a reconstruction. Recorded as `line_item_differs` by the 2026-09-05 provenance pass; no constant was retuned, and the target did not move because there is nothing to move it to.
The only rate-only Green Book row is FY2022's, and it is now carried beside this one as `biden_corporate_28_fy2022` — same reform, same factory, a per-point yield 36% lower.
credibility.caption: Out-of-sample accuracy, corporate: 4 pre-registered rows miss their published scores by 8.7% on average (median 8.4%), worst 13.4% — 2 of the 4 fall inside the average. On this figure that is -$1,053.1B to -$884.5B typical, -$1,098.6B to -$839.0B at the worst row. Read off the out-of-sample tier only — not the calibrated tiers, whose agreement is by construction. It is the observed spread of this model against published scores for this class of policy, not a confidence interval.
